react_result.final_narrative_text: Three independent enrichment paradigms converge on a single biological narrative: the arachidonic acid / eicosanoid axis is the dominant affected pathway. RaMP ORA (multi-database, hypergeometric) returned WP:WP167 'Eicosanoid synthesis' as the top-ranked pathway with an FDR of 3.16e-13 and a fold-enrichment of 1250.95, with five input metabolites (15-deoxy-Δ12,14-prostaglandin J2, arachidonic acid, 5-HETE, 15-HETE, leukotriene A4) hitting a 27-member pathway. The same five metabolites replicated across nine SMPDB drug-action sub-pathways at the same FDR, all driven by the identical lipid five-gene set. Mummichog's m/z-direct activity scan on the human_mfn empirical network identified 'Arachidonic acid metabolism' as its top hit (p = 0.0054, 11/11 input metabolites overlapping the 11-member network module) and 'Leukotriene metabolism' as rank 4 (p = 0.037), confirming network propagation from the same chemical neighbourhood. MetaboAnalystR KEGG PSEA placed KEGG:hsa00590 'Arachidonic acid metabolism' first, again populated by arachidonic acid, leukotriene A4, 15-HETE, and 5-HETE. The cross-paradigm consensus driver is arachidonic acid (KEGG:C00219), which sits at the metabolic entry point and feeds all downstream eicosanoid branches that produced the observed lipid mediators. Acetylcysteine (KEGG:C06809) and fructose 1-phosphate (KEGG:C01094) did not map to the eicosanoid cluster; they resolved to separate pathway hits in mummichog (glycerophospholipid metabolism, glycolysis/gluconeogenesis) consistent with antioxidant and central-carbon metabolism perturbations that are biologically distinct from the primary lipid signal. Dopamine (KEGG:C03758) mapped to tyrosine metabolism (KEGG:hsa00350) as a singleton hit. The convergent evidence across ORA and network-diffusion paradigms identifies eicosanoid biosynthesis as the primary affected pathway, with arachidonic acid as the central substrate driving the differential signal.

use run_ramp_enrichment (multi-DB ORA, broader namespace coverage) or run_metaboanalystr_psea (KEGG-specific ORA) instead
